findings.text: _published_image re-implements the published-image recogniser the repository already owns. The identical predicate (a 40-hex directory name plus a .complete marker) is inlined at reckon/checkout_trust.py:469 in running_code_identity, and the .complete half alone at reckon/crew_follow_commands.py:297, reckon/checkout_trust.py:229 and :484. The addition duplicates the owner rather than extending it, so a change to what marks a published image must now be made in a second place.

assert first != second cannot fail and does not guard the jitter it names: first is the doubled 120 s gap minus jitter and second is the 240 s gap minus jitter, so the two differ by 120 s even with the jitter removed entirely. The discriminating assertion is line 257 (assert 0.0 < first < first_gap), which reddens at zero jitter because first then equals first_gap; this test's durability rests on that line, not on line 266.

The gate command the manifest records does not name the node's own new test file: tests/test_a_moved_checkout_is_proved_importable_once.py is absent from the tests: line and no green head-arm log for it is stored in test_logs (only the mutated red arm, negative-control.log). The done_when's test bullets are the assertions in that file, so their pass is carried in artifacts as a claim rather than a recorded run; 10/10 were re-verified at head 167e407f4 during this review.

_record_import_verdict writes the verdict into the image directory and the lock file .import-probe.lock is created there too, while that directory's own mtime is the ranking key the pruner sorts by at reckon/checkout_trust.py:232 (_images_ranked_for_pruning). Proving an image therefore moves its retention rank; benign for the active image, but the proof and the retention order are coupled through one filesystem attribute that neither mechanism documents.
